extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for Area Chairs overseeing peer review for AISTATS 2025, covering responsibilities from initial checks and reviewer assignment through discussion facilitation and writing meta-reviews, plus policy and procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: OpenReview profile and registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure your profile on OpenReview is up-to-date. Adding your conflict of interests as well as selecting your expertise topics. Import papers to your OpenReview profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep conflicts and expertise current so assignment and contact functions work correctly; import assigned papers into your profile to facilitate monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agree to and follow Code of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Read and agree to abide by the AISTATS code of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professional, respectful behaviour is required throughout the review process; adhere to the conference code in all communications and actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify desk-rejection and conflict-of-interest cases
rubrics_metrics.description: After receiving the initial assignment, quickly check the submissions and identify desk-reject and/or conflict-of-interest cases if applicable. Examples: unacceptable formatting issues, dual submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag format violations and dual submissions early; consult FAQ for examples. If in doubt, mark as a violation so Program Chairs can review. Check for reproducibility checklist presence during author feedback (absence not automatic desk-reject).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper bidding and flexibility with expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Participate in bidding and accept that some assigned submissions may be outside your close expertise; be flexible and seek help from Senior AC if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a submission is too far from your expertise when making later decisions, contact Senior AC. Bidding and TPMS matching are used, so do initial checks promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer assignment and ensuring reviewer quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure every submission in your batch is matched with 5 suitable reviewers whom you can trust on this submission, ideally with a diverse set of opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest time before reviewing starts to recruit expert reviewers and adjust assignments. Recruit emergency reviewers if you lack enough high-quality reviews or if reviews diverge. Aim for reviewer expertise diversity to reduce borderline and mis-judged cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor reviewer responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor the review process and ensure reviewers are responsive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send reminders for on-time reviews; recruit emergency reviewers at least 1 week before review release if needed. If reviewers submit low-quality reviews, ask them to rewrite and resubmit. Be proactive to avoid missing deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure reviews provide evidence and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure reviewers provide their comments with evidence. E.g., if a reviewer selects “combinatorial approach” for novelty, ensure they provide corresponding references to justify this choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require that substantive claims in reviews are supported (references, concrete comparisons). Judge review quality by the content and evidence, not just the reviewer’s confidence score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitate author–reviewer discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that reviewers engage in discussions with the authors during the author-reviewer discussion period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage reviewers to at least acknowledge reading author comments and to indicate any score changes or lack thereof. Prompt reviewers to discuss with other reviewers to resolve misunderstandings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiate and lead reviewer–AC discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Initiate and lead discussions between reviewers after author feedback; read reviews and author feedback to understand pros/cons and major disagreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List points of contention in your discussion post; explicitly ask reviewers with very high/low scores to explain their opinions. Read confidential messages and, if needed, contact corresponding reviewers to address authors’ concerns without revealing confidential comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision making and timely meta-review submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Write meta-reviews on time and make acceptance/rejection recommendations based on the paper, reviews, author feedback, discussions, and your own understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meta-review must provide a convincing justification for the decision, especially rejections. The meta-review should augment reviews and explain how reviews, rebuttal, and discussions informed the recommendation. If uncertain, consult SAC early and discuss difficult cases with SAC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not ignore reviews or author feedback without explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not dismiss or ignore a review or author feedback unless you have a good reason; in such case you should also explain this in your meta review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you overrule or discount input, state the reasons in the meta-review. Transparency about what information you used (including any information not in the reviews) is required: tell authors that you used it and what it was.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide constructive feedback for rejected submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: For submissions with rejection decisions, you are encouraged to also provide comments regarding potential ways to improve the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer actionable suggestions to help authors improve; meta-reviews should be helpful and explainable to authors and program chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review content guidance (detailed standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on writing good meta-reviews: don’t focus too much on scores; judge review quality rather than confidence; compare reviewer keywords/expertise to authors' keywords; indicate whether the rebuttal addressed concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you wish to overrule unanimous reviewers, the standard for your summary should be at the level of a full review and solicit an auxiliary review if possible. Take a decisive stand on borderline papers. Try to counter reviewer biases (e.g., against unfashionable subjects) and recognize risk-taking work that may not yet be SOTA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommend oral presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend accepted submissions for oral talks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use your judgment and justification in meta-reviews to nominate papers suitable for oral presentation; provide rationale for recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolve issues and escalate appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolve any issue during the review process, e.g., by recruiting emergency reviewers, addressing concerns from reviewers and authors, and/or raising concerns with Senior ACs and Program Chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If encountering ethical or procedural problems, notify SAC and Program Chairs. Consult SAC before contacting other ACs/SACs about submissions assigned to you unless you have a justified reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best-practice professional conduct and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect deadlines and respond to emails as promptly as possible. It is okay to be unavailable briefly, but notify SAC if unavailable for extended periods (especially during critical windows).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be professional and considerate. If a reviewer cannot complete work, you may need to find an emergency reviewer or provide your own review. Exhibit empathy for personal situations affecting reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep everything relating to the review process confidential. Do not use ideas, code and results from submissions in your own work until they are publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not distribute submissions (code, ideas, results) without prior approval from program chairs. Do not talk about or distribute submissions to anyone without approval. Code submitted for reviewing cannot be distributed. Consult SAC/Program Chairs before discussing assigned submissions with other ACs/SACs.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM usage policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of LLMs is not allowed to write papers, reviews, and meta-reviews. They can be used as an assist tool, for example, to check grammatical issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You are responsible for any text you write, including content generated by LLMs that could be construed as plagiarism or scientific misconduct (e.g., fabrication of facts). LLMs are not eligible for authorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility checklist handling
rubrics_metrics.description: What if the paper does not have the reproducibility checklist? This does not count for desk-reject, although you should check whether the authors have submitted the checklist during author feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remind authors of accepted submissions to include the checklist in camera-ready.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limit and format violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Page limit: In the review period, the main part of the submission should be 8 pages long. After that, only the references are allowed. If that is not the case, please mark it as a format violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other format violations include anything that breaks anonymity, violates dual submission policy, changes the format (e.g., margins or vertical spaces). If in doubt, mark as a violation for Program Chairs to adjudicate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacting SAC and Program Chairs
rubrics_metrics.description: How to contact SAC and Program Chairs: use OpenReview contacting functions once assigned to an SAC; Program Chairs can be reached via the provided conference email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these channels for escalations, procedural questions, or to request assistance with difficult decisions or assignment issues.
